executive_summary: SD-LEARN-FIX-ADDRESS-PAT-LES-010 originated from /learn pattern PAT-LES-a7862f7339c4, which described a fragile stage22Data.promotion_gate.pass boolean check gating Stage 23's prerequisite kill gate. LEAD-phase verification (independently confirmed by an Explore sub-agent and a VALIDATION sub-agent) found this exact code no longer exists: it was superseded by an unrelated, later refactor (SD-LEO-INFRA-STAGE-TEMPLATE-DISPATCH-REMAINDER-001 renumbered Launch Readiness from stage-23.js to stage-24.js; SD-LEO-FEAT-STAGE-LAUNCH-READINESS-001 rewrote the Stage 22 prerequisite check entirely onto preflightUpstream(), a canonical venture_artifacts artifact-existence model with no boolean-coercion failure mode). Rather than reimplementing dead code, this SD delivers a permanent regression guard (a source-text test) proving the fragile shape can never silently reappear in the four relevant files, and updates the SD's own record to reflect the verified finding instead of the auto-generated, now-inaccurate boilerplate.

technical_requirements.title: Regression guard scope is deliberately narrow (literal-string check)
technical_requirements.description: The new guard test is a source-text literal-string match against exactly two strings (`stage22Data.promotion_gate`, `evaluateKillGate(`) in exactly four named files. It does NOT generalize to the broader class of boolean-coercion-fragile checks (e.g. a renamed variable `s22.promotion_gate?.pass !== true` would not be caught). This is an intentional, narrow guard against THIS specific historical regression, not a general-purpose coercion-safety linter -- do not describe it more broadly than that in any downstream documentation.
